For each file, find EVERY string that can reach a player's screen, and report it in the structured output. That includes:
- chat/console messages: game.print, player.print, force.print, surface.print
- flying text (player.create_local_flying_text etc.)
- GUI: caption=, tooltip=, text= on LuaGuiElement .add{} or assignments, including strings inside localised-string tables
- commands.add_command name + help text, and every response string those commands print
- custom alerts, message dialogs, set_goal_description, chart/map tag names, anything else display-bound
- data-stage: localised_name/localised_description, prototype names/descriptions, setting prototypes
- error() messages and log() calls (classify as category 'error'/'log', visibility 'log-only' or 'debug' as appropriate)
- strings handed to other mods or external systems (remote interface return values that get displayed, Discord bridge payloads) → category 'external'

Include even tiny strings ("OK", "Cancel", "+", "▶", "×"). For icon/symbol-only strings add hazard 'symbol-only'. Do NOT report: code comments, table keys, event/style/prototype identifier names used only as identifiers, file paths, pattern strings for string.find, storage keys.

Per string, set:
- status: 'localised' if it is already a {"section.key", ...} locale reference, 'partial' if a locale reference is concatenated/mixed with hardcoded English, 'hardcoded' otherwise.
- dynamic: describe exactly how it is assembled if not static — every '..' concatenation, string.format, table.concat, tick-to-time formatting, number formatting, player/team name interpolation. This is critical: concatenated sentences are the main localisation hazard.
- visibility: 'player' (any player sees it), 'admin' (admin-only), 'debug' (behind a debug flag), 'external' (leaves the game: Discord, RCON, files), 'log-only'.
- hazards, any of: 'concat' (sentence built by concatenation), 'plural' (text hardcodes singular/plural like "1 slot"/"slots" or picks between them in Lua), 'sentence-fragments' (reusable fragment strings composed into sentences elsewhere), 'rich-text' (embeds [color=]/[item=]/[font=] tags), 'server-side-string' (built into a plain Lua string before display, so all players would get one language), 'discord-mirror' (also sent to Discord/external where a LocalisedString cannot go), 'symbol-only', 'sorted-by-text' (list sorted by the display string), 'newlines' (embedded \n layout).

files_scanned must list every file you read (repo-relative), even ones with zero strings. In notes, mention anything structurally interesting for the localisation plan (helper functions that build messages, message pipelines, patterns repeated across files).

Your final output is consumed by a script, not a human — return only the structured data.

2	-- Categories, column caps, curated defaults, per-category item-list
3	-- resolution, and per-player panel state for the production stats GUI.
4	
5	local discovery = require("gui.stats.discovery")
6	
7	local M = {}
8	
9	-- ─── Constants ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
10	
11	-- MAX_COLS is the floor (minimum slots) for auto-discovered categories so
12	-- the table is never narrower than a vanilla layout. CURATED_COLS is the
13	-- cap for curated categories (intermediates, custom) — sized to give a few
14	-- empty trailing slots beyond the curated defaults for ad-hoc additions.
15	-- HARD_MAX_COLS is the ceiling for auto categories (overhaul mods can add
16	-- dozens of science packs / ores / plates).
17	M.MAX_COLS      = 12
18	M.CURATED_COLS  = 16
19	M.HARD_MAX_COLS = 48
20	
21	-- Categories whose item list comes from prototype scanning and should
22	-- auto-expand to fit every discovered item. Curated lists stay at CURATED_COLS.
23	local AUTO_CATEGORIES = { ores = true, plates = true, science = true }
24	
25	function M.is_auto_category(cat) return AUTO_CATEGORIES[cat] == true end
26	
27	local function cap_for(cat)
28	    return AUTO_CATEGORIES[cat] and M.HARD_MAX_COLS or M.CURATED_COLS
29	end
30	
31	M.CATEGORIES = {"ores", "plates", "intermediates", "science", "fluids", "custom"}
32	
33	M.CAT_LABELS = {
34	    ores          = "Ores",
35	    plates        = "Plates",
36	    intermediates = "Intermediates",
37	    science       = "Science",
38	    fluids        = "Fluids",
39	    custom        = "Custom",
40	}
41	
42	local DEFAULT_INTERMEDIATES = {
43	    "iron-gear-wheel", "copper-cable", "electronic-circuit", "advanced-circuit",
44	    "processing-unit", "pipe", "engine-unit", "electric-engine-unit",
45	    "flying-robot-frame", "battery", "low-density-structure",
46	    "rocket-fuel", "rocket-control-unit",
47	}
48	
49	local DEFAULT_CUSTOM = {"iron-plate", "steel-plate"}
50	
51	-- Curated fluid seeds (player request: crude oil, petroleum gas and
52	-- sulfuric acid pre-added, the rest player-editable). Each entry is
53	-- guarded by existence/visibility at resolution time, so a modpack
54	-- lacking any of them silently shows fewer.
55	local DEFAULT_FLUIDS = {
56	    "crude-oil", "petroleum-gas", "sulfuric-acid",
57	    "light-oil", "heavy-oil", "lubricant", "water", "steam",
58	}
59	
60	-- ─── Item List Resolution ──────────────────────────────────────────────
61	
62	local function default_item_names(cat)
63	    if cat == "fluids" then
64	        -- sort_fluids drops missing/hidden/parameter seeds; if a total
65	        -- conversion kills every seed, fall back to discovered fluids so
66	        -- the tab is never empty.
67	        local sorted = discovery.sort_fluids(DEFAULT_FLUIDS)
68	        if #sorted == 0 then sorted = discovery.all_visible_fluids() end
69	        local out = {}
70	        for _, entry in ipairs(sorted) do out[#out + 1] = entry.name end
71	        return out
72	    elseif cat == "intermediates" or cat == "custom" then
73	        local src = cat == "intermediates" and DEFAULT_INTERMEDIATES or DEFAULT_CUSTOM
74	        -- Sort curated lists by tech-unlock depth too, so the visual
75	        -- progression matches the auto-discovered tabs.
76	        local sorted = discovery.sort_by_unlock_depth(src)
77	        local out = {}
78	        for _, item in ipairs(sorted) do out[#out + 1] = item.name end
79	        return out
80	    else
81	        local cache = discovery.proto_lists()
82	        local items = cache[cat] or {}
83	        local out = {}
84	        for _, item in ipairs(items) do out[#out + 1] = item.name end
85	        return out
86	    end
87	end
88	
89	-- ─── Column records ────────────────────────────────────────────────────
90	
91	-- A column is a record {kind = "item"|"fluid", name = prototype-name}.
92	-- Existing saves hold bare item-name strings; coerce on read so no storage
93	-- migration is needed (PRODUCTION_STATS_PLAN.md, Data Model). Quality is
94	-- deliberately NOT a column field -- it is a view-level concern.
95	local function as_column(v)
96	    if type(v) == "string" then return {kind = "item", name = v} end
97	    return v
98	end
99	
100	-- Kind-aware existence check: a stale name (mod removed mid-save) drops
101	-- the column, matching the old prototypes.item[name] guard -- which would
102	-- otherwise silently drop every fluid column.
103	local function column_valid(col)
104	    if type(col) ~= "table" or not col.name then return false end
105	    if col.kind == "fluid" then return prototypes.fluid[col.name] ~= nil end
106	    return prototypes.item[col.name] ~= nil
107	end
108	
109	--- Returns a positional table of column records where nil means "empty
110	--- slot". For curated categories the array is capped at CURATED_COLS; for
111	--- auto categories it grows up to HARD_MAX_COLS so overhaul-mod prototypes
112	--- all get a slot. Respects per-player overrides in
113	--- storage.stats_category_items (records, or legacy name strings).
114	function M.get_columns(player_index, cat)
115	    local cap = cap_for(cat)
116	    local override = storage.stats_category_items
117	        and storage.stats_category_items[player_index]
118	        and storage.stats_category_items[player_index][cat]
119	    if override then
120	        local out = {}
121	        for i = 1, cap do
122	            local col = as_column(override[i])
123	            if column_valid(col) then out[i] = col end
124	        end
125	        return out
126	    end
127	    local defaults = default_item_names(cat)
128	    local kind = (cat == "fluids") and "fluid" or "item"
129	    local out = {}
130	    for i = 1, math.min(#defaults, cap) do
131	        out[i] = {kind = kind, name = defaults[i]}
132	    end
133	    return out
134	end
135	
136	--- Name-string view of get_columns -- the original public API shape, kept
137	--- for mod-compat callers via the gui/stats facade re-export.
138	function M.get_category_item_names(player_index, cat)
139	    local cols = M.get_columns(player_index, cat)
140	    local out = {}
141	    for i, col in pairs(cols) do out[i] = col.name end
142	    return out
143	end
144	
145	--- Column count the GUI should render for this category. Curated categories
146	--- stay at CURATED_COLS. Auto categories grow to fit all filled slots, with
147	--- one trailing empty slot for the user to add another item.
148	function M.get_target_cols(player_index, cat)
149	    if not AUTO_CATEGORIES[cat] then return M.CURATED_COLS end
150	    local items = M.get_columns(player_index, cat)
151	    local max_filled = 0
152	    for i = 1, M.HARD_MAX_COLS do
153	        if items[i] then max_filled = i end
154	    end
155	    local target = max_filled + 1
156	    if target < M.MAX_COLS      then target = M.MAX_COLS end
157	    if target > M.HARD_MAX_COLS then target = M.HARD_MAX_COLS end
158	    return target
159	end
160	
161	-- ─── Per-player panel state ────────────────────────────────────────────
162	
163	function M.get_state(player)
164	    if not storage.stats_gui_state then storage.stats_gui_state = {} end
165	    local s = storage.stats_gui_state[player.index]
166	    if not s then
167	        s = {
168	            category  = "ores",
169	            precision = defines.flow_precision_index.one_minute,
170	            quality   = "merged",
171	            sort_col  = nil,
172	            sort_dir  = "desc",
173	        }
174	        storage.stats_gui_state[player.index] = s
175	    end
176	    return s
177	end
178	
179	return M

25	    if n >= 1000000 then return string.format("%.1fM", n / 1000000) end
26	    if n >= 1000    then return string.format("%.1fk", n / 1000) end

31	--- over game.surfaces. The old per-cell get_count called
32	--- owned_surfaces_by_force per invocation, and get_owner's platform

34	--- teams x cols x surfaces x that before reading a single statistic.

36	--- so grouping by owner yields the same totals.

38	    local owned = {}
39	    for _, entry in ipairs(entries) do owned[entry.force.name] = {} end
40	    for _, surface in pairs(game.surfaces) do
41	        if surface.valid then
42	            local owner = surface_utils.get_owner(surface)
43	            local list = owner and owned[owner]
44	            if list then list[#list + 1] = surface end
45	        end
46	    end

71	---     merged by the gate). Multi cells expand once on the all-time axis
72	---     and read only qualities with real production -- sound because
73	---     counts are cumulative: all-time zero implies every window zero.
74	---
75	--- Returns (row_counts, breakdown, produced):
76	---   row_counts[row][col] = number, nil exactly at col_recs holes.
77	---   breakdown[row][col]  = {quality_name -> count} for merged-mode cells
78	---                          with non-normal production (tooltip data).
79	---   produced             = set of quality names seen with production
80	---                          across all rendered cells (selector row).
81	function M.collect(entries, col_recs, cols, precision, qview)
82	    qview = qview or "merged"
83	    local owned = surfaces_by_force(entries)
84	    local chain = quality.chain()
85	
86	    local has_fluid = false
87	    for col_idx = 1, cols do
88	        local col = col_recs[col_idx]
89	        if col and col.kind == "fluid" then has_fluid = true break end
90	    end
91	
92	    local req  = {name = nil, category = "input", precision_index = precision, count = true}
93	    local pair = {name = nil, quality = nil}
94	
95	    local row_counts, breakdown, produced = {}, {}, {}
96	    for i, entry in ipairs(entries) do
97	        local force  = entry.force
98	        local totals = {}
99	        local brk    = {}
100	        for col_idx = 1, cols do
101	            if col_recs[col_idx] then totals[col_idx] = 0 end
102	        end
103	        for _, surface in ipairs(owned[force.name]) do
104	            local ok, istats = pcall(force.get_item_production_statistics, surface)
105	            if ok and istats then
106	                if qview ~= "merged" then
107	                    -- Pinned view: one read per cell at that quality. No
108	                    -- gate, no breakdown -- the number IS one quality.
109	                    for col_idx = 1, cols do
110	                        local col = col_recs[col_idx]
111	                        if col and col.kind == "item" then
112	                            pair.name, pair.quality = col.name, qview
113	                            local ok2, val
114	                            if precision == M.ALLTIME then
115	                                ok2, val = pcall(istats.get_input_count, pair)
116	                            else
117	                                req.name = pair
118	                                ok2, val = pcall(istats.get_flow_count, req)
119	                            end
120	                            if ok2 and val then
121	                                totals[col_idx] = totals[col_idx] + val
122	                            end
123	                        end
124	                    end
125	                else
126	                    local okf, flat = pcall(read_input_counts, istats)
127	                    if okf and flat then
128	                        for col_idx = 1, cols do
129	                            local col = col_recs[col_idx]
130	                            -- kind dispatch: the fluid statistics path lands
131	                            -- with the Fluids tab (plan step 6).
132	                            if col and col.kind == "item" then
133	                                local merged_all = flat[col.name] or 0
134	                                local okn, normal_all = pcall(istats.get_input_count, col.name)
135	                                local multi = okn and normal_all ~= nil
136	                                    and merged_all ~= normal_all
137	
138	                                if precision == M.ALLTIME then
139	                                    totals[col_idx] = totals[col_idx] + merged_all
140	                                end
141	
142	                                if not multi then
143	                                    if precision ~= M.ALLTIME then
144	                                        req.name = col.name
145	                                        local ok2, val = pcall(istats.get_flow_count, req)
146	                                        if ok2 and val then
147	                                            totals[col_idx] = totals[col_idx] + val
148	                                        end
149	                                    end
150	                                else
151	                                    local cell_brk = brk[col_idx]
152	                                    if not cell_brk then
153	                                        cell_brk = {}
154	                                        brk[col_idx] = cell_brk
155	                                    end
156	                                    for _, qname in ipairs(chain) do
157	                                        pair.name, pair.quality = col.name, qname
158	                                        local oka, alltime = pcall(istats.get_input_count, pair)
159	                                        if oka and alltime and alltime > 0 then
160	                                            produced[qname] = true
161	                                            local val
162	                                            if precision == M.ALLTIME then
163	                                                val = alltime
164	                                            else
165	                                                req.name = pair
166	                                                local ok2, v = pcall(istats.get_flow_count, req)
167	                                                val = ok2 and v or nil
168	                                                if val then
169	                                                    totals[col_idx] = totals[col_idx] + val
170	                                                end
171	                                            end
172	                                            if val and val > 0 then
173	                                                cell_brk[qname] = (cell_brk[qname] or 0) + val
174	                                            end
175	                                        end
176	                                    end
177	                                end
178	                            end
179	                        end
180	                    end
181	                end
182	            end
183	        end
184	        -- Fluid columns: separate statistics object, bare-string IDs only
185	        -- ({name=...} parses as the Fluid concept and demands `amount` --
186	        -- probe D4/D5), fractional doubles, and NO quality axis: qview is
187	        -- ignored, a fluid cell always shows its full value (the panel
188	        -- hides the quality selector on the Fluids tab to match).
189	        if has_fluid then
190	            for _, surface in ipairs(owned[force.name]) do
191	                local okf2, fstats = pcall(force.get_fluid_production_statistics, surface)
192	                if okf2 and fstats then
193	                    if precision == M.ALLTIME then
194	                        local okd, flatf = pcall(read_input_counts, fstats)
195	                        if okd and flatf then
196	                            for col_idx = 1, cols do
197	                                local col = col_recs[col_idx]
198	                                if col and col.kind == "fluid" then
199	                                    totals[col_idx] = totals[col_idx] + (flatf[col.name] or 0)
200	                                end
201	                            end
202	                        end
203	                    else
204	                        for col_idx = 1, cols do
205	                            local col = col_recs[col_idx]
206	                            if col and col.kind == "fluid" then
207	                                req.name = col.name
208	                                local ok2, val = pcall(fstats.get_flow_count, req)
209	                                if ok2 and val then
210	                                    totals[col_idx] = totals[col_idx] + val
211	                                end
212	                            end
213	                        end
214	                    end
215	                end
216	            end
217	        end
218	
219	        row_counts[i] = totals
220	        breakdown[i]  = brk
221	    end
222	    return row_counts, breakdown, produced
223	end

13	
14	-- A prototype that exists and the modder has not flagged as hidden anywhere
15	-- the player-facing UI normally consults. Used to keep cross-mod stub items
16	-- (e.g. PM hiding vanilla production/utility/military science packs so
17	-- *other* mods can still wire them up) out of the column picker.

44	-- ─── Unlock depth ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────
45	
46	--- Computes, for every item, the depth at which it first becomes
47	--- producible. Recipe depth = (longest prerequisite chain to a root tech)
48	--- of the earliest tech that unlocks the recipe, or 0 if it's enabled at
49	--- game start. Item depth = min across *primary* producers (recipes where
50	--- the item is the main product, single-product recipes, or mining); if
51	--- the item has no primary producer anywhere, falls back to the min across
52	--- byproduct recipes. This keeps trace-byproduct paths from yanking items
53	--- to the front of the sort.
54	--- Fluid depth = min across ANY producing recipe (or 0 for resource
55	--- products like crude oil): no primary/byproduct split -- a byproduct
56	--- fluid (petroleum gas) is still how you get it.
57	local function compute_unlock_depths()
58	    local tech_depth = {}
59	    local function depth_of(tech_name, on_stack)
60	        local cached = tech_depth[tech_name]
61	        if cached ~= nil then return cached end
62	        local tech = prototypes.technology[tech_name]
63	        if not tech then return 0 end
64	        if on_stack[tech_name] then return 0 end -- cycle guard
65	        on_stack[tech_name] = true
66	        local max_d = 0
67	        for prereq_name in pairs(tech.prerequisites or {}) do
68	            local d = depth_of(prereq_name, on_stack) + 1
69	            if d > max_d then max_d = d end
70	        end
71	        on_stack[tech_name] = nil
72	        tech_depth[tech_name] = max_d
73	        return max_d
74	    end
75	
76	    -- Pass 1: derive each recipe's depth. A recipe gets the *minimum* depth
77	    -- across all techs that unlock it. If a recipe is never unlocked by any
78	    -- tech but is enabled by default, its depth is 0 (available from game
79	    -- start). Recipes that are neither enabled-by-default nor tech-unlocked
80	    -- are unreachable and are skipped entirely.
81	    local recipe_unlock_depth = {}
82	    for tech_name, tech in pairs(prototypes.technology) do
83	        local d = depth_of(tech_name, {})
84	        for _, effect in pairs(tech.effects) do
85	            if effect.type == "unlock-recipe" then
86	                local cur = recipe_unlock_depth[effect.recipe]
87	                if not cur or d < cur then
88	                    recipe_unlock_depth[effect.recipe] = d
89	                end
90	            end
91	        end
92	    end
93	
94	    -- Pass 2: split producers into "primary" (this recipe is canonically how
95	    -- the item is made) and "byproduct" (the item just happens to fall out
96	    -- of a recipe whose main output is something else). A recipe is primary
97	    -- for an item iff main_product names that item, or the recipe has
98	    -- exactly one item product (single-output recipes have no ambiguity).
99	    -- Mining is the canonical "primary" producer for ore-style items, at
100	    -- depth 0.
101	    local primary_depth, byproduct_depth, fluid_depth = {}, {}, {}
102	
103	    for _, entity in pairs(prototypes.entity) do
104	        if entity.type == "resource" and entity.mineable_properties then
105	            for _, product in pairs(entity.mineable_properties.products or {}) do
106	                if product.type == "item" then
107	                    primary_depth[product.name] = 0
108	                elseif product.type == "fluid" then
109	                    fluid_depth[product.name] = 0
110	                end
111	            end
112	        end
113	    end
114	
115	    for recipe_name, recipe in pairs(prototypes.recipe) do
116	        local rd = recipe_unlock_depth[recipe_name]
117	        if rd == nil and recipe.enabled then rd = 0 end
118	        if rd ~= nil then
119	            local item_products, fluid_products = {}, {}
120	            for _, product in pairs(recipe.products) do
121	                if product.type == "item" then
122	                    item_products[#item_products + 1] = product.name
123	                elseif product.type == "fluid" then
124	                    fluid_products[#fluid_products + 1] = product.name
125	                end
126	            end
127	            for _, name in ipairs(fluid_products) do
128	                local cur = fluid_depth[name]
129	                if not cur or rd < cur then fluid_depth[name] = rd end
130	            end
131	            -- main_product has a documented third state at the data stage:
132	            -- the empty string (= explicitly no main product). Treat it as
133	            -- nil so it can never accidentally match a product name.
134	            local main_name = recipe.main_product and recipe.main_product.name or nil
135	            if main_name == "" then main_name = nil end
136	            for _, name in ipairs(item_products) do
137	                local is_primary
138	                if main_name then
139	                    is_primary = (name == main_name)
140	                else
141	                    -- Sole product of the WHOLE recipe, not sole item: a
142	                    -- one-item + one-fluid recipe with no main_product
143	                    -- (barrel emptying) is ambiguous, and counting only
144	                    -- items let barrels inherit early unlock depths.
145	                    -- Measured: exactly the 7 barrel-emptying recipes
146	                    -- change, none of which feed the auto tabs.
147	                    is_primary = (#item_products == 1 and #fluid_products == 0)
148	                end
149	                local target = is_primary and primary_depth or byproduct_depth
150	                local cur = target[name]
151	                if not cur or rd < cur then target[name] = rd end
152	            end
153	        end
154	    end
155	
156	    -- Primary always wins. Byproduct depth is only used for items that have
157	    -- no primary producer anywhere (otherwise a trace byproduct unlocked
158	    -- early would outrank the item's canonical recipe and yank it to the
159	    -- front of the sort).
160	    local item_depth = {}
161	    for name, d in pairs(primary_depth)   do item_depth[name] = d end
162	    for name, d in pairs(byproduct_depth) do
163	        if item_depth[name] == nil then item_depth[name] = d end
164	    end
165	    return {items = item_depth, fluids = fluid_depth}
166	end

168	local function get_depths()
169	    if depth_cache then return depth_cache end
170	    depth_cache = compute_unlock_depths()
171	    return depth_cache
172	end

174	-- Order a list of item names by tech-unlock depth, with the prototype's
175	-- group/item order as a tiebreaker. Drops items the modder has hidden.
176	function M.sort_by_unlock_depth(names)
177	    local depths = get_depths().items
178	    local list = {}
179	    for _, name in ipairs(names) do
180	        if is_visible_item(name) then
181	            local proto = prototypes.item[name]

185	                depth = depths[name] or 0,
186	                tie   = g .. proto.order,
187	            }
188	        end
189	    end

191	        if a.depth ~= b.depth then return a.depth < b.depth end
192	        return a.tie < b.tie
193	    end)
194	    return list
195	end

199	--- The ores / plates / science item lists discovered from prototypes,

219	            end
220	        end
221	    end

1	-- gui/stats/quality.lua
2	-- Quality-chain discovery for the production stats GUI.
3	--
4	-- The chain MUST be walked via .next from "normal" -- both obvious
5	-- alternatives fail on real modpacks (measured, see
6	-- docs/PRODUCTION_STATS_PROBES.md):
7	--   * level-sort: levels run 0,1,2,3,5,6,7,8,10 with Quality-Plus-Plus
8	--     (gaps at 4/9), and the unreachable "quality-unknown" placeholder
9	--     also reports level 0, tying with normal.
10	--   * hidden-filter: base ships normal.hidden = true (the quality mod
11	--     flips it back), so a base-only install would drop "normal" itself.
12	-- The walk also excludes quality-unknown for free: nothing links to it.
13	
14	local M = {}
15	
16	-- Rebuilt each script load (prototype set is fixed per load; a mod change
17	-- reloads control.lua, so no storage cache or invalidation is needed).
18	local chain_cache = nil
19	
20	--- Ordered quality names, walking .next from "normal". The docs declare
21	--- .next non-optional but it is genuinely nil-terminated -- `while q do`
22	--- is the correct loop, never `while q.next do`.
23	function M.chain()
24	    if chain_cache then return chain_cache end
25	    local out, seen = {}, {}
26	    local q = prototypes.quality["normal"]
27	    while q and not seen[q.name] do
28	        seen[q.name] = true
29	        out[#out + 1] = q.name
30	        q = q.next
31	    end
32	    -- A pack without a "normal" prototype is out-of-contract for the base
33	    -- game; fall back to a bare normal so statistics reads stay callable.
34	    if #out == 0 then out[1] = "normal" end
35	    chain_cache = out
36	    return chain_cache
37	end
38	
39	--- True when the quality axis is worth surfacing at all: feature flag on
40	--- and more than one quality in the chain. Base-only installs get false
41	--- and the panel renders exactly as it always did.
42	function M.multi_enabled()
43	    return script.feature_flags.quality and #M.chain() > 1
44	end
45	
46	return M
47

292	--- Handle GUI clicks. Returns true if consumed.

294	    local el = event.element
295	    if not (el and el.valid) then return false end
296	
297	    if el.name == "sb_team_settings_close" then
298	        local player = game.get_player(event.player_index)
299	        if player then team_settings.close(player) end
300	        return true

303	    if el.name == "sb_team_settings_rename" then

306	        -- Save button and textfield share the same name_row parent.
307	        local field = el.parent and el.parent.sb_team_settings_name
308	        if field and field.valid then
309	            do_rename(player, field.text)

311	        return true
312	    end

314	    if el.name == "sb_team_settings_lfm_toggle" then
315	        -- Any team member can toggle recruiting (not just the leader).
316	        local player = game.get_player(event.player_index)
317	        if not (player and is_on_team(player)) then return true end
318	        local force_name = player.force.name
319	        storage.team_looking_for_more = storage.team_looking_for_more or {}
320	        local now_lfm = not storage.team_looking_for_more[force_name]
321	        storage.team_looking_for_more[force_name] = now_lfm or nil
322	        if now_lfm then
323	            storage.lfm_ever_recruited = storage.lfm_ever_recruited or {}
324	            storage.lfm_ever_recruited[force_name] = true
325	            lfm_hint.close(player)
326	            helpers.broadcast("[Team] " .. helpers.team_tag(force_name)
327	                .. " is looking for more players!")
328	        else
329	            helpers.broadcast("[Team] " .. helpers.team_tag(force_name)
330	                .. " is no longer recruiting.")
331	        end

333	        pen_gui.update_pen_gui_all()
334	        return true
335	    end
336	
337	    return false

359	        counter.style.font = at_limit and "default-bold" or "default"
360	        counter.style.font_color = at_limit and {1, 0.4, 0.4} or {0.7, 0.7, 0.7}
361	    end
362	    return true
363	end
